detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 501
According to section 501 of Indian penal code, Whoever prints or engraves any matter, knowing or having good reason to believe that such matter is defamatory of any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simple_explanation: If someone prints or engraves any content, knowing or having good reason to believe that it is defamatory about a person, they can be punished with up to two years of simple imprisonment, a fine, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found printing or engraving matter knowing it to be defamatory against the president or the vice-president or the governor of a state or administrator of a union territory or a minister in respect of his conduct in the discharge of his public functions when instituted upon a complaint made by the public prosecutor, they would be held accountable under this section and face simple imprisonment for 2 years or fine or both.
punishment: Simple Imprisonment for 2 Years or Fine or Both

title: Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing it to contain such matter against the President or the Vice-President or the Governor of a State or Administrator of a Union territory or a Minister in respect of his conduct in the discharge of his public functions when instituted upon a complaint made by the Public Prosecutor
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 502
According to section 502 of Indian penal code, Whoever sells or offers for sale any printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing that it contains such matter, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simple_explanation: If someone knowingly sells or offers for sale any printed or engraved material containing defamatory content, they can be punished with up to two years of simple imprisonment, a fine, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing it to contain such matter against the president or the vice-president or the governor of a state or administrator of a union territory or a minister in respect of his conduct in the discharge of his public functions when instituted upon a complaint made by the public prosecutor, they would be held accountable under this section and face simple imprisonment for 2 years or fine or both.
punishment: Simple Imprisonment for 2 Years or Fine or Both

title: nan
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 503
According to section 503 of Indian penal code, Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person, or to cause that person to do any act which he is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do any act which that person is legally entitled to do, as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat, commits criminal intimidation.
simple_explanation: Criminal intimidation is when someone threatens another with harm to their person, reputation, or property, intending to cause fear or coerce them into doing something they are not legally required to do or refraining from an act they have a legal right to do.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found nan, they would be held accountable under this section and face nan.

title: Insult intended to provoke breach of the peace
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 504
According to section 504 of Indian penal code, Whoever intentionally insults, and thereby gives provocation to any person, intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause him to break the public peace, or to commit any other offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
simple_explanation: If someone intentionally insults another person, knowing it could provoke them to disturb public peace or commit another offense, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found insult intended to provoke breach of the peace, they would be held accountable under this section and face 2 years or fine or both.

title: False statement, rumour, etc., circulated with intent to cause mutiny or offence against the public peace
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 505
According to section 505 of Indian penal code,
Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement, rumour or report
with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or
with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against the public tranquility; or
with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit any offence against any other class or community, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Statements creating or promoting enmity, hatred or ill will between classes
Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing rumour or alarming news with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
Offence under sub-section (2) committed in place of worship, etc.
Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
simple_explanation: Whoever makes or circulates statements or rumors with intent to cause mutiny or fear among military personnel, incite offenses against the State or public tranquility, or promote hatred between different religious or social groups can be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with a fine, or both; and if committed in a place of worship, the punishment can extend up to five years with a fine.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found false statement, rumour, etc., circulated with intent to cause mutiny or offence against the public peace, they would be held accountable under this section and face 3 years or fine or both.

title: Criminal intimidation
simple_explanation: If someone commits the offense of criminal intimidation, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both; and if the threat involves serious harm, destruction of property by fire, or imputing unchastity to a woman, the punishment can extend to seven years of imprisonment, a fine, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found criminal intimidation, they would be held accountable under this section and face 2 years or fine or both.

title: Criminal intimidation by Anonymous communication or having taken precaution to conceal whence the threat comes
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 507
According to section 507 of Indian penal code, Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or having taken precaution to conceal the name or abode of the person from whom the threat comes, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to the punishment provided for the offence by the last preceding section.
simple_explanation: If someone engages in criminal intimidation using an anonymous communication or hides their identity to issue threats, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, along with the punishment prescribed for the offense of criminal intimidation.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found criminal intimidation by anonymous communication or having taken precaution to conceal whence the threat comes, they would be held accountable under this section and face as in section 506 + 2 years.

title: Act caused by inducing a person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 508
According to section 508 of Indian penal code, Whoever voluntarily causes or attempts to cause any person to do anything which that person is not legally bound to do, or to omit to do anything which he is legally entitled to do, by inducing or attempting to induce that person to believe that he or any person in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered by some act of the offender an object of Divine displeasure if he does not do the thing which it is the object of the offender to cause him to do, or if he does the thing which it is the object of the offender to cause him to omit, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
simple_explanation: If someone tries to make another person do something they are not legally obligated to do or refrain from something they are legally entitled to do by falsely claiming that divine displeasure will befall them or someone they care about, they can be punished with up to one year of imprisonment, a fine, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found act caused by inducing a person to believe that he will be rendered an object of divine displeasure, they would be held accountable under this section and face 1 year or fine or both.

title: Uttering any word or making any gesture intended to insult the modesty of a woman, etc.
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 509
According to section 509 of Indian penal code, Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
simple_explanation: If someone intentionally tries to insult a woman's modesty by using offensive words, gestures, or actions, or intrudes on her privacy, they can be punished with up to three years of simple imprisonment, along with a fine.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found uttering any word or making any gesture intended to insult the modesty of a woman, etc., they would be held accountable under this section and face simple imprisonment for 3 years + fine.

title: Appearing in a public Place, etc., in a State of intoxication, and causing annoyance to any person
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 510
According to section 510 of Indian penal code, Whoever, in a state of intoxication, appears in any public place, or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty-four hours, or with fine which may extend to ten rupees, or with both.
simple_explanation: If someone, while intoxicated, behaves in a way that annoys others in a public or restricted area, they can be punished with up to 24 hours of simple imprisonment, or a fine up to ten rupees, or both.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found appearing in a public place, etc., in a state of intoxication, and causing annoyance to any person, they would be held accountable under this section and face simple imprisonment for 24 hours or fine or both.
punishment: Simple Imprisonment for 24 hours or Fine or Both

title: Attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment, and in such attempt doing any act towards the commission of the offence
detailed_explanation:
Description of IPC Section 511
According to section 511 of Indian penal code, Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall, where no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such attempt, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.
simple_explanation: Whoever tries to commit a crime punishable by imprisonment or causes someone else to commit it, but fails, can be punished with imprisonment up to half the maximum term or a fine, as specified for that offense.
real_life_example: For instance, if a person is found attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment, and in such attempt doing any act towards the commission of the offence, they would be held accountable under this section and face imprisonment for life or imprisonment not exceeding, half of the longest term provided for the offence, or fine, or both.
punishment: Imprisonment for Life or Imprisonment not exceeding, half of the longest term provided for the Offence, or Fine, or Both

title: Name and territory of the Union
detailed_explanation: Establishes that India, also known as Bharat, is a Union of States. It defines the territory of India as comprising the territories of the States, the Union territories, and any other territories that may be acquired.
simple_explanation: Establishes that India, also known as Bharat, is a Union of States. It defines the territory of India as comprising the territories of the States, the Union territories, and any other territories that may be acquired.
real_life_example: When a new state like Telangana is formed, its territory becomes a part of the Union under this article.

title: Admission or establishment of new States
detailed_explanation: Empowers Parliament to admit new states into the Union of India or establish new states on terms and conditions it deems fit.
simple_explanation: Empowers Parliament to admit new states into the Union of India or establish new states on terms and conditions it deems fit.
real_life_example: The admission of Pondicherry (Puducherry) into the Union of India as a territory.

title: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
detailed_explanation: Allows Parliament to form a new state by separation, union, or alteration of the territory, area, boundaries, or names of existing states, provided the President refers the proposal to the concerned state legislature for its views.
simple_explanation: Allows Parliament to form a new state by separation, union, or alteration of the territory, area, boundaries, or names of existing states, provided the President refers the proposal to the concerned state legislature for its views.
real_life_example: The reorganization of Andhra Pradesh to form the state of Telangana in 2014.

title: Laws made under articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedules and supplemental, incidental and consequential matters
detailed_explanation: Mandates that any reorganization or admission laws made under Articles 2 and 3 must include provisions to amend the First Schedule (list of states) and Fourth Schedule (allocation of Rajya Sabha seats) without requiring a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
simple_explanation: Mandates that any reorganization or admission laws made under Articles 2 and 3 must include provisions to amend the First Schedule (list of states) and Fourth Schedule (allocation of Rajya Sabha seats) without requiring a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
real_life_example: When Jharkhand was created, the First and Fourth Schedules were automatically updated via the reorganization act.

title: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
detailed_explanation: Grants citizenship at the launch of the Constitution to any person domiciled in India who was born in India, had a parent born in India, or had been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years preceding the commencement.
simple_explanation: Grants citizenship at the launch of the Constitution to any person domiciled in India who was born in India, had a parent born in India, or had been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years preceding the commencement.
real_life_example: A person living in Delhi since 1944 became an Indian citizen automatically on January 26, 1950.

title: Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan
detailed_explanation: Provides citizenship rights to persons who migrated from Pakistan to India prior to the start of the Constitution, establishing a permit and cutoff date system of July 19, 1948.
simple_explanation: Provides citizenship rights to persons who migrated from Pakistan to India prior to the start of the Constitution, establishing a permit and cutoff date system of July 19, 1948.
real_life_example: Refugees who crossed the Pakistan-India border in September 1947 and lived in India became citizens under this provision.

title: Rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan
detailed_explanation: Overrules Articles 5 and 6, stating that persons who migrated from India to Pakistan after March 1, 1947, lose their Indian citizenship unless they returned under a valid resettlement permit.
simple_explanation: Overrules Articles 5 and 6, stating that persons who migrated from India to Pakistan after March 1, 1947, lose their Indian citizenship unless they returned under a valid resettlement permit.
real_life_example: A person who moved to Lahore in April 1947 but returned to India under a permanent resettlement permit in 1949 remains an Indian citizen.

title: Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India
detailed_explanation: Secures citizenship for persons of Indian origin residing outside India (such as diplomats or ex-pats), provided they register with the diplomatic/consular representative of India in that country.
simple_explanation: Secures citizenship for persons of Indian origin residing outside India (such as diplomats or ex-pats), provided they register with the diplomatic/consular representative of India in that country.
real_life_example: An Indian origin merchant living in London who registers at the Indian High Commission in London.

title: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens
detailed_explanation: Strictly prohibits dual citizenship; any Indian citizen who voluntarily acquires foreign state citizenship automatically loses their Indian citizenship.
simple_explanation: Strictly prohibits dual citizenship; any Indian citizen who voluntarily acquires foreign state citizenship automatically loses their Indian citizenship.
real_life_example: An Indian citizen obtaining United States citizenship in 2020 automatically forfeits their Indian passport and citizenship.

title: Continuance of the rights of citizenship
detailed_explanation: Guarantees that every person deemed to be a citizen of India under this Part continues to be a citizen, subject to any law made by Parliament.
simple_explanation: Guarantees that every person deemed to be a citizen of India under this Part continues to be a citizen, subject to any law made by Parliament.
real_life_example: Indian citizens have a persistent status that cannot be arbitrarily stripped except by standard parliamentary legislation.

title: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
detailed_explanation: Grants plenary power to Parliament to legislate on the acquisition and termination of citizenship, and all other related matters.
simple_explanation: Grants plenary power to Parliament to legislate on the acquisition and termination of citizenship, and all other related matters.
real_life_example: The enactment of the Citizenship Act, 1955, and its subsequent amendments like the CAA.

title: Definition of State
detailed_explanation: Defines 'the State' for Part III (Fundamental Rights) to include the Government and Parliament of India, state governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities.
simple_explanation: Defines 'the State' for Part III (Fundamental Rights) to include the Government and Parliament of India, state governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities.
real_life_example: Municipal corporations, LIC, ONGC, and nationalized banks are considered 'the State' under this definition.

title: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights
detailed_explanation: Provides for judicial review by declaring that any pre-existing or post-constitutional laws that violate or abridge fundamental rights shall be null and void to the extent of their inconsistency.
simple_explanation: Provides for judicial review by declaring that any pre-existing or post-constitutional laws that violate or abridge fundamental rights shall be null and void to the extent of their inconsistency.
real_life_example: A law passed by a state state banning free speech without reasonable grounds would be declared void under this article.

title: Equality before law
detailed_explanation: Guarantees that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India, prohibiting arbitrary class legislation.
simple_explanation: Guarantees that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India, prohibiting arbitrary class legislation.
real_life_example: Rich and poor people are tried in the same criminal justice system for committing the same offense.

title: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
detailed_explanation: Prohibits the State and citizens from discriminating against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth regarding access to public places, wells, and hotels.
simple_explanation: Prohibits the State and citizens from discriminating against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth regarding access to public places, wells, and hotels.
real_life_example: A public restaurant cannot deny entry to a person based on their caste or gender.

title: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
detailed_explanation: Ensures equal opportunity for all citizens in employment or appointment to offices under the State, prohibiting discrimination.
simple_explanation: Ensures equal opportunity for all citizens in employment or appointment to offices under the State, prohibiting discrimination.
real_life_example: In a civil services exam, candidates are evaluated based on merit and cannot be excluded merely because of their state of origin.

title: Abolition of Untouchability
detailed_explanation: Abolishes the practice of 'Untouchability' in any form and declares the enforcement of any disability arising from it to be an offense punishable by law.
simple_explanation: Abolishes the practice of 'Untouchability' in any form and declares the enforcement of any disability arising from it to be an offense punishable by law.
real_life_example: Preventing a person from entering a temple or drawing water from a public well based on untouchability is forbidden and highly illegal.
punishment: No punishment directly in Constitution, but enforced via the Protection of Civil Rights Act and SC/ST Act, which contain punishments.

title: Abolition of titles
detailed_explanation: Prohibits the State from conferring any title (except military or academic distinctions) and prevents Indian citizens from accepting titles from foreign states.
simple_explanation: Prohibits the State from conferring any title (except military or academic distinctions) and prevents Indian citizens from accepting titles from foreign states.
real_life_example: An Indian citizen cannot use royal titles like 'Sir', 'Maharaja', or 'Rai Bahadur' given by a government.

title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
detailed_explanation: Guarantees six essential freedoms to all citizens: speech and expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations/unions, free movement, residence, and practicing any profession/trade.
simple_explanation: Guarantees six essential freedoms to all citizens: speech and expression, peaceful assembly, forming associations/unions, free movement, residence, and practicing any profession/trade.
real_life_example: Protesting peacefully without arms or starting a business venture/startup anywhere in India.

title: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
detailed_explanation: Provides three critical protections to accused persons: protection against ex-post facto laws (no retroactive criminal laws), double jeopardy (cannot be punished twice for the same offense), and self-incrimination (cannot be forced to witness against oneself).
simple_explanation: Provides three critical protections to accused persons: protection against ex-post facto laws (no retroactive criminal laws), double jeopardy (cannot be punished twice for the same offense), and self-incrimination (cannot be forced to witness against oneself).
real_life_example: Police cannot use a confession extracted under physical torture as the sole basis of conviction in a court trial.

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
detailed_explanation: Declares that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This has been expanded to include rights to privacy, clean air, livelihood, and medical care.
simple_explanation: Declares that no person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This has been expanded to include rights to privacy, clean air, livelihood, and medical care.
real_life_example: A person cannot face capital punishment or state detention without a comprehensive and fair judicial process.

title: Right to education
detailed_explanation: Mandates the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in a manner determined by state law.
simple_explanation: Mandates the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in a manner determined by state law.
real_life_example: The execution of the Right to Education (RTE) Act of 2009, enabling children from poor backgrounds to attend primary schools.

title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
detailed_explanation: Provides procedural safeguards for arrested persons, including the right to know grounds of arrest, consult a lawyer of choice, and be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
simple_explanation: Provides procedural safeguards for arrested persons, including the right to know grounds of arrest, consult a lawyer of choice, and be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
real_life_example: When a suspect is arrested, police must present them to the nearest local magistrate court within one full day of custody.

title: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
detailed_explanation: Strictly prohibits human trafficking, 'begar' (forced labor without payment), and other similar forms of compelled labor, making violations punishable offences.
simple_explanation: Strictly prohibits human trafficking, 'begar' (forced labor without payment), and other similar forms of compelled labor, making violations punishable offences.
real_life_example: Bonded laborers forced to work in brick kilns to repay ancestral debts are liberated under this constitutional mandate.

title: Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
detailed_explanation: Explicitly bans children under the age of fourteen years from being employed to work in any factory, mine, or other hazardous industries.
simple_explanation: Explicitly bans children under the age of fourteen years from being employed to work in any factory, mine, or other hazardous industries.
real_life_example: Employing a twelve-year-old child to work inside a firecracker factory is a severe violation.

title: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
detailed_explanation: Guarantees to all persons freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate their chosen religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
simple_explanation: Guarantees to all persons freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate their chosen religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
real_life_example: A person organizing a religious discourse or wearing a religious symbol (such as sikhs carrying a kirpan) is fully protected.

title: Freedom to manage religious affairs
detailed_explanation: Grants religious denominations or sections the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious/charitable purposes, manage their own religious affairs, and own/administer property in accordance with law.
simple_explanation: Grants religious denominations or sections the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious/charitable purposes, manage their own religious affairs, and own/administer property in accordance with law.
real_life_example: A religious trust running temple assets, managing festivals, and maintaining dharamshalas legally.

title: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
detailed_explanation: Prohibits the State from compelling any person to pay taxes if the proceeds are specifically used to promote or maintain any particular religion or religious denomination.
simple_explanation: Prohibits the State from compelling any person to pay taxes if the proceeds are specifically used to promote or maintain any particular religion or religious denomination.
real_life_example: Government tax funds cannot be exclusively allocated to build a shrine or mosque of one specific sect.

title: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions
detailed_explanation: Bans religious instructions in educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds. It allows religious instructions in institutions administered by State but established under a trust, while making attendance optional for state-recognized/aided schools.
simple_explanation: Bans religious instructions in educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds. It allows religious instructions in institutions administered by State but established under a trust, while making attendance optional for state-recognized/aided schools.
real_life_example: A government-run primary school cannot mandate catechism or religious prayers of a single faith for its students.

title: Protection of interests of minorities
detailed_explanation: Protects the cultural and language rights of minorities, stating any section of Indian citizens having a distinct language, script, or culture has the right to conserve it, and bars state-aided institutions from denying entry based on religion, race, or caste.
simple_explanation: Protects the cultural and language rights of minorities, stating any section of Indian citizens having a distinct language, script, or culture has the right to conserve it, and bars state-aided institutions from denying entry based on religion, race, or caste.
real_life_example: Groups seeking to preserve traditional dialects like Santhali or tribal scripts are constitutionally protected.

title: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
detailed_explanation: Grants all religious and linguistic minorities the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, protecting them from state discrimination in granting monetary aid.
simple_explanation: Grants all religious and linguistic minorities the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, protecting them from state discrimination in granting monetary aid.
real_life_example: Christian, Sikh, or Muslim minority trusts running collegiate institutions with reserved seat systems for their communities.

title: Saving of laws providing for acquisition of estates, etc.
detailed_explanation: Saves state acquisition laws (like agrarian land land reform laws) from being declared void under Article 14 or 19 to simplify economic reforms.
simple_explanation: Saves state acquisition laws (like agrarian land land reform laws) from being declared void under Article 14 or 19 to simplify economic reforms.
real_life_example: State land acquisition acts taking over agricultural estates to redistribute them to landless peasants.

title: Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
detailed_explanation: Protects laws placed in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution from being declared void for violating fundamental rights, subject to judicial review of the basic structure.
simple_explanation: Protects laws placed in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution from being declared void for violating fundamental rights, subject to judicial review of the basic structure.
real_life_example: Placing certain agrarian land tenure laws under the Ninth Schedule to prevent judicial challenges.

title: Saving of laws giving effect to certain directive principles
detailed_explanation: Protects laws giving effect to certain Directive Principles (Articles 39(b) and (c)) from being declared null and void on the grounds of violating Articles 14 or 19.
simple_explanation: Protects laws giving effect to certain Directive Principles (Articles 39(b) and (c)) from being declared null and void on the grounds of violating Articles 14 or 19.
real_life_example: Nationalizing key natural mineral wealth to share resources equitably among citizens.

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
detailed_explanation: Grants the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights. It also empowers the Supreme Court to issue highly functional writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari.
simple_explanation: Grants the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights. It also empowers the Supreme Court to issue highly functional writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari.
real_life_example: Filing a public interest litigation (PIL) or writ petition when an individual is unlawfully detained by police.

title: Power of Parliament to modify the rights conferred by this Part in their application to Forces, etc.
detailed_explanation: Authorizes Parliament to limit or abrogate the fundamental rights of members of the Armed Forces, paramilitary forces, police, and intelligence agencies to ensure discipline and proper discharge of duty.
simple_explanation: Authorizes Parliament to limit or abrogate the fundamental rights of members of the Armed Forces, paramilitary forces, police, and intelligence agencies to ensure discipline and proper discharge of duty.
real_life_example: Limiting soldiers of the Indian Army from forming political unions or addressing media without permission.

title: Restriction on rights conferred by this Part while martial law is in force in any area
detailed_explanation: Enables Parliament to restrict fundamental rights in any area where martial law (military rule) is actively in force and indemnify any state officer for actions taken to restore order.
simple_explanation: Enables Parliament to restrict fundamental rights in any area where martial law (military rule) is actively in force and indemnify any state officer for actions taken to restore order.
real_life_example: Indemnifying soldiers acting to maintain peace in an active territory placed under coordinate military control.

title: Legislation to give effect to the provisions of this Part
detailed_explanation: Confers exclusive legislative power to Parliament, to the exclusion of state legislatures, to make laws implementing fundamental rights and prescribing punishments for violations.
simple_explanation: Confers exclusive legislative power to Parliament, to the exclusion of state legislatures, to make laws implementing fundamental rights and prescribing punishments for violations.
real_life_example: Only Parliament could enact the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act or laws defining residence requirements.

title: Definition of State in Part IV
detailed_explanation: Provides that the term 'the State' under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) has the exact same definition as found in Part III (Article 12).
simple_explanation: Provides that the term 'the State' under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) has the exact same definition as found in Part III (Article 12).
real_life_example: Local municipal councils are also bound to follow Directive Principles when crafting local developmental schemes.

title: Application of the principles contained in this Part
detailed_explanation: Declares that the Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the nation and must guide policymaking.
simple_explanation: Declares that the Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the nation and must guide policymaking.
real_life_example: A citizen cannot sue the government in court because a village does not have a local employment scheme, as it is non-justiciable.

title: State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to promote the welfare of people by securing a social order characterized by social, economic, and political justice, and specifically striving to minimize inequalities in income and opportunities.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to promote the welfare of people by securing a social order characterized by social, economic, and political justice, and specifically striving to minimize inequalities in income and opportunities.
real_life_example: The introduction of schemes like affordable housing, subsidies, and free healthcare to reduce economic inequality.

title: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
detailed_explanation: Instructs the State to optimize its policies to secure adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of resources, equal pay for equal work for both men and women, and protection of child health.
simple_explanation: Instructs the State to optimize its policies to secure adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of resources, equal pay for equal work for both men and women, and protection of child health.
real_life_example: Crafting maternity leave benefits and legislative acts securing equal wage distribution for casual laborers.

title: Equal justice and free legal aid
detailed_explanation: Requires the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity and to provide free legal aid by schemes or legislation to backward or disabled citizens.
simple_explanation: Requires the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity and to provide free legal aid by schemes or legislation to backward or disabled citizens.
real_life_example: The creation of Legal Services Authorities (like NALSA) to provide free legal consultations to vulnerable accused individuals.

title: Organisation of village Panchayats
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to organize village panchayat structures and endow them with necessary power and authority to act as decentralized units of self-government.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to organize village panchayat structures and endow them with necessary power and authority to act as decentralized units of self-government.
real_life_example: This led historically to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act legalizing rural local bodies across India.

title: Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
detailed_explanation: Directs the State within its economic capacity limits to make effective provisions securing the right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, and sickness.
simple_explanation: Directs the State within its economic capacity limits to make effective provisions securing the right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, and sickness.
real_life_example: The launch of the MGNREGA scheme securing 100 days of guaranteed work for rural households.

title: Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to secure just and humane work environments for employees and provide comprehensive maternity relief schemes.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to secure just and humane work environments for employees and provide comprehensive maternity relief schemes.
real_life_example: The enactment of the Maternity Benefit Act of 1961 providing dynamic paid leave for working women.

title: Living wage, etc., for workers
detailed_explanation: Strives to provide a living wage, standard work environments, leisure opportunities, and promotion of cottage industries on individual or cooperative bases in rural areas.
simple_explanation: Strives to provide a living wage, standard work environments, leisure opportunities, and promotion of cottage industries on individual or cooperative bases in rural areas.
real_life_example: Establishing cottage industry boards like Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

title: Participation of workers in management of industries
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to take steps by suitable legislation to secure the participation of workers in the management of industrial undertakings and organizations.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to take steps by suitable legislation to secure the participation of workers in the management of industrial undertakings and organizations.
real_life_example: Creating works committees or employee board seats in nationalized manufacturing public undertakings.

title: Promotion of co-operative societies
detailed_explanation: Urges the State to encourage voluntary formation, autonomous operations, democratic controls, and professional management of co-operative societies.
simple_explanation: Urges the State to encourage voluntary formation, autonomous operations, democratic controls, and professional management of co-operative societies.
real_life_example: Supporting the formation and growth of Amul dairy cooperative structures.

title: Uniform civil code for the citizens
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to endeavour to secure for all citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) regarding personal laws like marriage, divorce, and succession throughout India.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to endeavour to secure for all citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) regarding personal laws like marriage, divorce, and succession throughout India.
real_life_example: Goa has a Uniform Civil Code, which is historically derived, and discussions continue regarding national implementation.

title: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years
detailed_explanation: Instructs the State to prioritize extending early childhood care and education to all children until they complete six years of age.
simple_explanation: Instructs the State to prioritize extending early childhood care and education to all children until they complete six years of age.
real_life_example: The functioning of Anganwadi centers under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme.

title: Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic prospects of the weaker sections of people, particularly SCs and STs, protecting them from exploitation.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic prospects of the weaker sections of people, particularly SCs and STs, protecting them from exploitation.
real_life_example: Extending special education scholarships or coaching grants to SC and ST students.

title: Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to elevate the level of nutrition and standard of living of its people, treat public health as a primary duty, and bring about prohibition of injurious drinks and drugs.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to elevate the level of nutrition and standard of living of its people, treat public health as a primary duty, and bring about prohibition of injurious drinks and drugs.
real_life_example: Banning dangerous narcotics or state governments choosing to implement total liquor bans (like in Bihar or Gujarat).

title: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern, scientific lines, improve breeds, and take steps to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and draught cattle.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern, scientific lines, improve breeds, and take steps to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and draught cattle.
real_life_example: Drafting cattle preservation laws across various states banning the slaughter of cows and calves.

title: Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to endeavour to protect and improve the natural environment and safeguard the forest ecosystems and wildlife of the nation.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to endeavour to protect and improve the natural environment and safeguard the forest ecosystems and wildlife of the nation.
real_life_example: The direct enactment of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and establishing Reserved National Forests.

title: Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
detailed_explanation: Places a strict constitutional obligation on the State to protect artistic or historic monuments declared of national importance from spoliation, destruction, export, or disfigurement.
simple_explanation: Places a strict constitutional obligation on the State to protect artistic or historic monuments declared of national importance from spoliation, destruction, export, or disfigurement.
real_life_example: The Archaelogical Survey of India (ASI) managing and restoring the Taj Mahal or Red Fort.

title: Separation of judiciary from executive
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to take active steps to separate the judicial branch from the executive offices in the public services to ensure judicial independence.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to take active steps to separate the judicial branch from the executive offices in the public services to ensure judicial independence.
real_life_example: District magistrates do not conduct judicial trials; this is handled solely by judicial magistrates belonging to independent legal cadres.

title: Promotion of international peace and security
detailed_explanation: Directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international laws, and encourage settling international disputes by arbitration.
simple_explanation: Directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international laws, and encourage settling international disputes by arbitration.
real_life_example: India participating in United Nations peace missions or solving bilateral boundary disputes peacefully via arbitration tribunals.

title: Fundamental duties
detailed_explanation: Provides a comprehensive list of eleven fundamental duties of every Indian citizen, including respecting the Constitution, defending the nation, preserving environmental systems, and providing educational opportunities to wards aged 6-14.
simple_explanation: Provides a comprehensive list of eleven fundamental duties of every Indian citizen, including respecting the Constitution, defending the nation, preserving environmental systems, and providing educational opportunities to wards aged 6-14.
real_life_example: Standing up in respect during the national anthem or keeping public monuments free from litter.
punishment: No punishment directly, but several statutes like prevention of insults to national honor act carry punishments.

title: The President of India
detailed_explanation: Establishes the executive office of the President, declaring, 'There shall be a President of India'.
simple_explanation: Establishes the executive office of the President, declaring, 'There shall be a President of India'.
real_life_example: The President acts as the nominal titular head of state, executing official deeds.

title: Executive power of the Union
detailed_explanation: Vests the supreme executive power of the Union in the President, to be exercised directly or through subordinate officers. It also vests the supreme command of defense forces in the President.
simple_explanation: Vests the supreme executive power of the Union in the President, to be exercised directly or through subordinate officers. It also vests the supreme command of defense forces in the President.
real_life_example: All official executive orders of the central government are formally executed in the President's name.

title: Election of President
detailed_explanation: Mandates that the President of India shall be elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
simple_explanation: Mandates that the President of India shall be elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
real_life_example: A nominated Rajya Sabha member cannot vote in the election of the President, only elected members are eligible.

title: Manner of election of President
detailed_explanation: Lays down the formula for the presidential election, following the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote via secret ballot to ensure uniformity.
simple_explanation: Lays down the formula for the presidential election, following the system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote via secret ballot to ensure uniformity.
real_life_example: Applying value calculations for votes cast by MLAs and MPs during the official tally.

title: Term of office of President
detailed_explanation: Establishes a 5-year tenure for the President from the date they enter office. Lays down standard resignation processes and impeachment references under Article 61.
simple_explanation: Establishes a 5-year tenure for the President from the date they enter office. Lays down standard resignation processes and impeachment references under Article 61.
real_life_example: A President may submit a hand-written resignation to the Vice-President of India.

title: Eligibility for re-election
detailed_explanation: Declares that a person who holds or has held the office of the President is eligible for re-election to that office, with no ceiling on terms.
simple_explanation: Declares that a person who holds or has held the office of the President is eligible for re-election to that office, with no ceiling on terms.
real_life_example: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was re-elected as President, fully permitted by this article.

title: Qualifications for election as President
detailed_explanation: Requires any presidential candidate to be an Indian citizen, aged at least thirty-five years, qualified for election as a member of the House of the People, and not hold any office of profit.
simple_explanation: Requires any presidential candidate to be an Indian citizen, aged at least thirty-five years, qualified for election as a member of the House of the People, and not hold any office of profit.
real_life_example: A 32-year old citizen cannot stand for presidential elections as they do not meet the age requirement.

title: Conditions of President's office
detailed_explanation: States the President cannot be a member of either House of Parliament or a State Legislature. If elected, they vacate their legislative seat. They are entitled to rent-free official residences, and their emoluments cannot be diminished during their term.
simple_explanation: States the President cannot be a member of either House of Parliament or a State Legislature. If elected, they vacate their legislative seat. They are entitled to rent-free official residences, and their emoluments cannot be diminished during their term.
real_life_example: The President's salary and usage of Rashtrapati Bhavan cannot be abridged or cut mid-tenure.

title: Oath or affirmation by the President
detailed_explanation: Requires the President to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Chief Justice of India, promising to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution.
simple_explanation: Requires the President to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Chief Justice of India, promising to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution.
real_life_example: The formal oath-taking ceremony on Rashtrapati Bhavan lawns in the presence of the CJI.

title: Procedure for impeachment of the President
detailed_explanation: Delineates the rigorous procedure for removing the President by impeachment for 'violation of the Constitution', requiring resolutions initiated by a 1/4th notice and passed by a 2/3rd majority of either house.
simple_explanation: Delineates the rigorous procedure for removing the President by impeachment for 'violation of the Constitution', requiring resolutions initiated by a 1/4th notice and passed by a 2/3rd majority of either house.
real_life_example: If a President actively violates constitutional commands, Parliament moves an impeachment resolution.
punishment: No punishment directly, but results in removal from office.

title: Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy
detailed_explanation: Mandates that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of President must be completed before the term expires, and casual vacancies (death, resignation) must be filled within six months.
simple_explanation: Mandates that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of President must be completed before the term expires, and casual vacancies (death, resignation) must be filled within six months.
real_life_example: If a president resigns, a fresh election is legally mandated to be conducted within six months.

title: The Vice-President of India
detailed_explanation: Establishes the permanent office of the Vice-President, stating, 'There shall be a Vice-President of India'.
simple_explanation: Establishes the permanent office of the Vice-President, stating, 'There shall be a Vice-President of India'.
real_life_example: The Vice-President acts as the second-highest constitutional officer.

title: The Vice-President to be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States
detailed_explanation: Requires the Vice-President of India to perform the duties of the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), prohibiting them from holding any other office of profit.
simple_explanation: Requires the Vice-President of India to perform the duties of the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), prohibiting them from holding any other office of profit.
real_life_example: The Vice-President presiding over debates and votes in the Rajya Sabha chamber.

title: The Vice-President to act as President or to discharge his functions during casual vacancies in the office, or during the absence, of President
detailed_explanation: Empowers the Vice-President to fulfill the duties or act as the President in case of death, resignation, illness, or absence of the President, enjoying all presidential immunities and salaries.
simple_explanation: Empowers the Vice-President to fulfill the duties or act as the President in case of death, resignation, illness, or absence of the President, enjoying all presidential immunities and salaries.
real_life_example: If the President goes abroad or falls ill, the Vice-President formally assumes acting duties.

title: Election of Vice-President
detailed_explanation: Establishes that the Vice-President shall be elected by members of an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, utilizing proportional representation.
simple_explanation: Establishes that the Vice-President shall be elected by members of an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, utilizing proportional representation.
real_life_example: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha members voting via secret secret ballot for Vice-President.

title: Term of office of Vice-President
detailed_explanation: Assigns a 5-year tenure to the Vice-President. Outlines resignation paths and removal through a simple majority resolution passed in the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
simple_explanation: Assigns a 5-year tenure to the Vice-President. Outlines resignation paths and removal through a simple majority resolution passed in the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
real_life_example: The Rajya Sabha initiates a removal resolution after providing a mandatory fourteen days' notice.

title: Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of Vice-President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy
detailed_explanation: Declares that elections to fill a regular vacancy in the office of Vice-President must be completed before their tenure ends, and casual vacancies must be filled as soon as possible.
simple_explanation: Declares that elections to fill a regular vacancy in the office of Vice-President must be completed before their tenure ends, and casual vacancies must be filled as soon as possible.
real_life_example: Conducting elections when a Vice-President is reaching the end of their five-year term.

title: Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President
detailed_explanation: Requires every Vice-President to make an oath or affirmation before the President of India to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India.
simple_explanation: Requires every Vice-President to make an oath or affirmation before the President of India to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India.
real_life_example: The President administering the oath of office in the Durbar Hall.

title: Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies
detailed_explanation: Allows Parliament to make any statutory provisions it deems fit to discharge presidential functions in unforeseen contingencies not explicitly covered in the Constitution.
simple_explanation: Allows Parliament to make any statutory provisions it deems fit to discharge presidential functions in unforeseen contingencies not explicitly covered in the Constitution.
real_life_example: Enacting the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969, enabling the Chief Justice of India to act as President.

title: Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President
detailed_explanation: Vests exclusive jurisdiction in the Supreme Court to inquire and decide on all doubts and disputes regarding the election of the President or Vice-President, making its rulings final.
simple_explanation: Vests exclusive jurisdiction in the Supreme Court to inquire and decide on all doubts and disputes regarding the election of the President or Vice-President, making its rulings final.
real_life_example: A challenge to the election process of a President is adjudicated directly by the Supreme Court.

title: Power of President to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases
detailed_explanation: Confers sovereign power on the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute sentences in cases of military court martial, Union subjects, or death sentences.
simple_explanation: Confers sovereign power on the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute sentences in cases of military court martial, Union subjects, or death sentences.
real_life_example: Commuting a death sentence given in a murder trial into rigorous life imprisonment.

title: Extent of executive power of the Union
detailed_explanation: Establishes that the executive power of the Union extends to all matters on which Parliament is competent to pass legislation and to the exercise of rights under international treaties.
simple_explanation: Establishes that the executive power of the Union extends to all matters on which Parliament is competent to pass legislation and to the exercise of rights under international treaties.
real_life_example: The central government carrying out national highways maintenance or signing foreign commercial treaties.

title: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
detailed_explanation: Establishes a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. It protects the advice from judicial inquiry.
simple_explanation: Establishes a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice. It protects the advice from judicial inquiry.
real_life_example: The President must sign bills and issue declarations as advised by the Prime Minister in Cabinet meetings.

title: Other provisions as to Ministers
detailed_explanation: Directs that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice, the Cabinet is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and restricts their total count to 15% of Lok Sabha seats.
simple_explanation: Directs that the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice, the Cabinet is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and restricts their total count to 15% of Lok Sabha seats.
real_life_example: An MP loses minister status if they fail to win a seat in either house within six consecutive months.

title: Attorney-General for India
detailed_explanation: Directs the President to appoint a person qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court as the Attorney-General for India, acting as the chief legal advisor to the government.
simple_explanation: Directs the President to appoint a person qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court as the Attorney-General for India, acting as the chief legal advisor to the government.
real_life_example: The Attorney-General presenting arguments in court on behalf of the central government during challenging litigation.

title: Conduct of business of the Government of India
detailed_explanation: Requires all executive actions of the central government to be expressed in the name of the President, and authorizes rules for allocating business among ministers.
simple_explanation: Requires all executive actions of the central government to be expressed in the name of the President, and authorizes rules for allocating business among ministers.
real_life_example: Signing of an international commercial agreement by the government as 'in the name of the President'.

title: Duties of Prime Minister as respects the furnishing of information to the President, etc.
detailed_explanation: Mandates that the Prime Minister must communicate all decisions of the Cabinet regarding Union administration and legislative proposals to the President, and submit items pin-pointed by the President.
simple_explanation: Mandates that the Prime Minister must communicate all decisions of the Cabinet regarding Union administration and legislative proposals to the President, and submit items pin-pointed by the President.
real_life_example: The Prime Minister regularly briefs the President on security matters and planned acts.

title: Constitution of Parliament
detailed_explanation: Establishes Parliament for the Union, consisting of the President and two Houses to be known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
simple_explanation: Establishes Parliament for the Union, consisting of the President and two Houses to be known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
real_life_example: The passing of national legislation requires the consent of Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and the President.

title: Composition of the Council of States
detailed_explanation: Defines the composition of the Rajya Sabha to consist of not more than 250 members, including 12 members nominated by the President for excellence in literature, science, art, or social service, and representatives of states.
simple_explanation: Defines the composition of the Rajya Sabha to consist of not more than 250 members, including 12 members nominated by the President for excellence in literature, science, art, or social service, and representatives of states.
real_life_example: Nominating a renowned scientist or artist to a Rajya Sabha seat.

title: Composition of the House of the People
detailed_explanation: Defines the composition of the Lok Sabha, consisting of not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States, and up to 20 representing Union territories.
simple_explanation: Defines the composition of the Lok Sabha, consisting of not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States, and up to 20 representing Union territories.
real_life_example: Conducting direct voting in a local constituency during national Lok Sabha elections.

title: Readjustment after each census
detailed_explanation: Mandates the delimitation and reallocation of seats in the Lok Sabha among states and divisions after every official census report is published.
simple_explanation: Mandates the delimitation and reallocation of seats in the Lok Sabha among states and divisions after every official census report is published.
real_life_example: Updating constituency bound lines after census numbers are completed.

title: Duration of Houses of Parliament
detailed_explanation: Declares Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution (with 1/3rd retiring every two years) and Lok Sabha has a 5-year tenure unless dissolved earlier.
simple_explanation: Declares Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution (with 1/3rd retiring every two years) and Lok Sabha has a 5-year tenure unless dissolved earlier.
real_life_example: When a national emergency is in force, Parliament can extend the Lok Sabha's term by up to 1 year at a time.

title: Qualification for membership of Parliament
detailed_explanation: Prescribes candidate requirements to sit in Parliament: citizen of India, must take official oath, at least age thirty for Rajya Sabha, and at least age twenty-five for Lok Sabha.
simple_explanation: Prescribes candidate requirements to sit in Parliament: citizen of India, must take official oath, at least age thirty for Rajya Sabha, and at least age twenty-five for Lok Sabha.
real_life_example: A 26-year-old citizen is constitutionally qualified to run as a candidate for the Lok Sabha.

title: Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution
detailed_explanation: Authorizes the President to summon either House of Parliament, provided that more than six months do not intervene between sessions. It also allows the President to prorogue or dissolve Lok Sabha.
simple_explanation: Authorizes the President to summon either House of Parliament, provided that more than six months do not intervene between sessions. It also allows the President to prorogue or dissolve Lok Sabha.
real_life_example: Summoning of Winter or Budget Sessions by the President.

title: Right of President to address and send messages to Houses
detailed_explanation: Grants the President the authority to address either House of Parliament or send messages regarding any pending bills.
simple_explanation: Grants the President the authority to address either House of Parliament or send messages regarding any pending bills.
real_life_example: The President sending a crucial message regarding an urgent national administrative matter.

title: Special address by the President
detailed_explanation: Requires the President to address both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
simple_explanation: Requires the President to address both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.
real_life_example: The President's annual speech detailing government plans at the start of the budget session.

title: Rights of Ministers and Attorney-General as respects Houses
detailed_explanation: Entitles every minister and the Attorney-General of India to speak and participate in the proceedings of either House or joint sittings, without any right to vote.
simple_explanation: Entitles every minister and the Attorney-General of India to speak and participate in the proceedings of either House or joint sittings, without any right to vote.
real_life_example: The Attorney-General speaking in the Lok Sabha relative to challenging legal concepts.

title: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
detailed_explanation: Reiterates the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, and mandates Rajya Sabha to choose a member as Deputy Chairman.
simple_explanation: Reiterates the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, and mandates Rajya Sabha to choose a member as Deputy Chairman.
real_life_example: The election of a deputy chairman to manage Rajya Sabha sessions.

title: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the office of Deputy Chairman
detailed_explanation: Outlines conditions under which the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman vacates office, resigns, or is removed by a simple majority resolution.
simple_explanation: Outlines conditions under which the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman vacates office, resigns, or is removed by a simple majority resolution.
real_life_example: Sumbiting a resignation letter addressed to the Rajya Sabha Chairman.

title: Power of the Deputy Chairman or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Chairman
detailed_explanation: Empowers the Deputy Chairman or nominee to perform duties of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha if the Chairman's office is vacant or they are acting as President.
simple_explanation: Empowers the Deputy Chairman or nominee to perform duties of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha if the Chairman's office is vacant or they are acting as President.
real_life_example: The Deputy Chairman managing sessions when the Vice-President is sick.

title: The Chairman or the Deputy Chairman not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration
detailed_explanation: Bars the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha from presiding over sessions when a resolution for their removal is active.
simple_explanation: Bars the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha from presiding over sessions when a resolution for their removal is active.
real_life_example: Another chosen member presides while Rajya Sabha debates removing the Deputy Chairman.

title: Repeals
detailed_explanation: Formally repeals the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, on the commencement of the Constitution.
simple_explanation: Formally repeals the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, on the commencement of the Constitution.
real_life_example: This marked the complete formal release of sovereign India from colonial-era constitutional frameworks.
